选举日期可以被质疑，但不能被政治阴谋化

针对有人批评选委会把柔佛与森美兰州选安排在不同日期投票，甚至指控选委会“故意阻止游子投票”，我认为这个说法需要更理性地看待。

监督选委会是必要的。
要求选委会解释，也是民主社会应有的权利。

但是，监督不等于可以直接定罪；质疑不等于可以制造阴谋论。

柔佛与森美兰虽然解散州议会日期接近，但这并不代表两州选举一定必须在同一天投票。

选举安排涉及选民人数、投票中心、选务人员、安全部署、行政准备、地方情况以及后勤协调，不是简单一句“相差几天解散，为什么不同步投票”就能下结论。

尤其柔佛是大州，选民人数庞大，又涉及大量跨境工作者、交通流量、关卡压力和地方行政安排。选委会当然应该说明理由，也应该交代标准，但在没有证据证明违法或故意针对某一群选民之前，直接指控选委会“存心阻止投票”，这是过度政治化。

至于所谓“星期六投票就是卡死新加坡游子”，这个说法也不完整。

星期六投票确实可能影响部分在新加坡工作的选民，尤其是轮班、服务业、制造业和无法轻易请假的工作群体。这个问题必须被正视。

但是，星期日投票也不是完全没有问题。很多游子可能星期日投票后要赶回新加坡，关卡交通、回程压力、工作安排同样会成为负担。

所以，问题的核心不是简单地说“星期六一定错，星期日一定对”，而是政府和选委会有没有提供更完整的配套。

真正应该推动的是：

改善新柔关卡通关安排；
加强投票日前后的交通协调；
改善邮寄投票机制；
提供更清楚的游子投票指南；
协调雇主与相关单位给予投票便利；
让选民能够更容易、更有尊严地履行公民责任。

这才是解决问题。

如果真的关心游子投票，就应该提出实际方案，而不是只用“45万游子被卡死”这样的标题制造愤怒。

我们要问的是：
如何让更多人回来投票？
如何降低投票成本？
如何改善边境交通？
如何让选举制度更便利？
如何让选委会更透明？

而不是一开始就把问题推向“有人故意阻止人民投票”。

政治最怕的不是批评，而是没有证据的动机论。

今天任何政党、任何政治人物、任何评论者，都有权批评选委会。但批评必须有事实基础，必须有逻辑一致性，也必须提出解决方案。

如果每一个行政决定都被包装成政治阴谋，最后受伤的不是某个机构，而是人民对民主制度的信任。

选委会必须透明。
政治人物也必须负责任。

可以要求解释，不能任意定罪。
可以要求改革，不能消费情绪。
可以关心游子，不能利用游子。

马来西亚政治已经不能继续停留在标题党、情绪战和标签化攻击。

人民要的不是更多愤怒。
人民要的是更好的制度、更便利的投票、更成熟的政治，以及真正能解决问题的治理能力。

-刘天球@13 June 2026

The wisdom and independence of the Election Commission of Malaysia (SPR) are commendable.
 
The Election Commission’s decision to hold the Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections separately is highly praiseworthy.
 
This is far more than a mere administrative arrangement of election dates. It is a decision that embodies institutional wisdom, constitutional awareness, administrative prudence, and a mature grasp of Malaysia’s political landscape.
 
This arrangement is significant and judicious for the following reasons:
 
First, Negeri Sembilan is currently embroiled in sensitive political and royal-related disputes. Amid such a delicate situation, elections must not become a catalyst for heightened constitutional uncertainties or political tensions. By deferring polling for Negeri Sembilan, the SPR has created a much-needed buffer zone, allowing issues in the state to be resolved in a calmer and more orderly manner. This is not political meddling, but a demonstration of sound constitutional awareness.
 
Second, the decision grants Negeri Sembilan a cooling-off period. When political sentiments run high and institutions are under strain, allowing time to pass is itself an act of responsible governance. A hasty election would risk turning state-level constitutional disputes into full-blown political confrontation. Postponing the Negeri Sembilan state election eases undue political pressure and enables democratic proceedings to take place in a more stable environment.
 
Third, this move affords all political parties and candidates fair and ample time for preparation. A well-run election entails far more than polling day alone. It covers nomination preparations, campaign organisation, voter outreach, manifesto dissemination, logistical planning, oversight mechanisms, law enforcement coordination and public communication. By allocating sufficient lead time, the SPR upholds the principle of fair competition among all contestants.
 
Fourth, the arrangement reflects the SPR’s administrative prudence. Organising elections is a massive logistical and administrative undertaking, involving election officials, security personnel, ballot printing, polling station setup, postal and early voting, staff training, media liaison and regulatory supervision. Holding the two major state elections separately alleviates administrative burdens and minimises operational risks. This is not delay, but effective risk management.
 
Fifth, the decision embodies a voter-centric approach. Voters need time to comprehend relevant issues so as to make well-considered choices. Johor and Negeri Sembilan face distinct political environments, local concerns and electoral dynamics. Separate polls allow voters in each state to focus on their own local priorities, rather than being swept up by a single national political narrative. This is a testament to respect for voters’ right to informed decision-making.
 
Sixth, and most importantly, the decision showcases the institutional independence of the SPR. A truly independent election body does not merely follow procedures mechanically. It must strike a balance between legal frameworks, administrative constraints, political realities and public interests. Through this arrangement, the SPR has proven its capacity to make judgements based on accountability and institutional maturity.
 
This decision deserves recognition, for it strengthens public confidence in the electoral system. Democracy is not just about holding elections; more crucially, it requires elections to be conducted in a fair, credible and stable manner that earns public trust.
 
The SPR has demonstrated wisdom.
The SPR has demonstrated independence.
The SPR has demonstrated a strong sense of responsibility.
 
Fair elections demand adequate time.
Stable democracy relies on wisdom.
Credible democracy requires an independent election commission.
 
 -Ronnie Liu Tian Khiew
